stops.stop: Institut de France, the ratio
stops.date_confidence: attested that Poisson worked from matter as molecules interacting through central forces and derived relations among the elastic constants, including the transverse to longitudinal strain ratio now called his; the paper 'Sur l'extension des fils et des plaques élastiques' is of 1827, in the Annales de chimie et de physique, and the elasticity work runs to 1831, so 1828 here is an ordering date. The universal value the molecular theory implies is given as 1/2 by Kosmann-Schwarzbach, SIGMA 18 (2022) 092, and as 1/4 by the standard elasticity literature, where the case of equal Lamé parameters is still called a Poisson solid; the contradiction is recorded and not resolved. Kosmann-Schwarzbach also states that the variability of the ratio across materials had been established experimentally by engineers before the 1970s and lacked theoretical grounding until then, which is the reverse of what the dossier said. The closing sentence, on Lakes 1987, postdates Poisson and is flagged for the operator in the report. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from evariste_galois.journey.json.
